**Finding: compliant (preferred position met).**

Commerce One imposes no non-compete or field-of-use covenant on Corio:

- **No restrictive covenant anywhere.** Searches for "compete", "exclusive", "restriction", "covenant" and "Corio shall not" surface only nonexclusive licence grants, the §2.7 software-use restrictions, arbitration/severability wording and a covenant not to sue — nothing barring Corio from developing, marketing or selling competing products, and no post-term restraint.
- **Licence-scope limits are not non-competes.** The Territory (§1.11, North America), Corio Market Segment (§1.3, customers under $1B) and the §2.1 "no licence … for use other than as part of the Corio Services" language define the scope of Commerce One's grant of its own Software; they do not restrict Corio's business, products or customers generally. §2.10 further allows Corio to seek worldwide expansion at no additional cost.
- **Independent development expressly preserved.** §13.6: "Nothing in this Agreement will be construed to prohibit either parties' right to independently develop the Developments contemplated above."

No redline proposed — the clause set sits at our preferred position, so there is nothing to negotiate on this rule.
